verdict.rationale: Warp's marketing says it supports jobs that run 'when something happens,' and that users can write their own, which is a first-party event-triggered automation capability. The only evidence is one marketing line, with no documentation of how rules or triggers are defined. Webhooks only notify an external endpoint, so they are a developer building block and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documented rule/trigger definition (supported event types, conditions, actions), AI-native rule authoring, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Jobs that run on a schedule or when something happens. Defaults are on, and you can write your own.
